headline: Ansar Allah claim ballistic-missile hit on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (550,000 bpd), Saudi authorities do not confirm'
dek: ATTRIBUTED REPORT, NOT A VERIFIED HIT: Saree said the Ansar Allah targeted the Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile, causing a fire / 'massive fires' at the complex, which includes a shipping terminal on the Gulf west of the Strait of Hormuz. sources: Ansar Allah military spokesperson Yahya Saree (statement, via Reuters/AFP); Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki (Riyadh intercept, via AFP/Gulf News); Bloomberg unnamed person familiar (fire near terminal containe
fault_line: Hit or hype: did a Ansar Allah missile actually set Ras Tanura alight, or is an unconfirmed claim plus a contained terminal fire being read as a refinery strike?

sections.what_happened: ATTRIBUTED REPORT, NOT A VERIFIED HIT: Saree said the Ansar Allah targeted the Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile, causing a fire / 'massive fires' at the complex, which includes a shipping terminal on the Gulf west of the Strait of Hormuz. Ras Tanura capacity is 550,000 barrels per day and it is the kingdom's biggest refinery; nearly all Saudi oil exports flow through Ras Tanura (Gulf) and Yanbu (Red Sea). Saudi authorities did NOT immediately confirm the strike. Bloomberg, cited by Reuters, reported via a person familiar with the matter that Saudi Arabia had contained a fire near Ras Tanura's terminal in the early hours -- that corroborates a fire near the terminal, NOT a confirmed missile hit on the refinery or damage scale. SEPARATE TUESDAY-AFTERNOON EVENT (not the 0700-01 wave): the coalition said air defences intercepted and destroyed 2 ballistic missiles launched by the Ansar Allah toward Riyadh on Tuesday afternoon; Saudi Civil Defence issued alerts for Riyadh, al-Kharj, al-Hariq, Abha, Khamis Mushait and Najran, later saying the danger had passed. This Riyadh pair is DISTINCT from the 0700-01 wave (3 missiles Eastern Region + 4 drones Southern Region, 02:17 UTC). Saree also claimed, via Jerusalem Post/Reuters, hits on the Saudi Defence Ministry and Abha airport -- those two claims have no Saudi confirmation in-window and are recorded as claims only. NOT A FIRST: Ansar Allah Ras Tanura claims recur (an Oct 24 Alghad TV post in the engagement set lists a Ras Tanura claim among 7 claimed operations; Reuters notes Ras Tanura was attacked by the Ansar Allah in 2021) -- the Oct 27 claim is new as a dated statement, not a first-ever attack claim.
sections.what_verified: Ansar Allah claim carried by Reuters (T1) and AFP (T1, via Malay Mail); the contained-fire-near-terminal detail via Bloomberg (T1, unnamed source, via Reuters); the Riyadh intercept via the coalition statement carried by AFP (T1, via Dawn) and Gulf News liveblog. Jerusalem Post, Straits Times and radio-site carries are the same Reuters text, NOT additional families.
sections.what_disputed: Saudi authorities did not confirm the Ras Tanura strike; no damage, casualty or shutdown figure for the refinery was confirmed in-window. Social comments on the claim are sharply polarized and sceptical in part -- Al Jazeera graphic commenters question the spokesperson's status and demand video proof, and call the image AI-generated/recycled -- that is commenter scepticism, NOT evidence about the strike, and must not be presented as a debunk. The fire Bloomberg cites is 'near the terminal', not a confirmed refinery hit.
sections.why_matters: '550,000 BARRELS IN THE CROSSHAIRS' -- the Ansar Allah claim a missile fire at Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery; Riyadh says it stopped 2 missiles aimed at the capital. Claim, non-confirmation and the contained-fire report all on screen, nothing asserted beyond them.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Reuters Oct 27 11:29 UTC = 15:29 ; in no prior scan) -- Ansar Allah claim ballistic-missile hit on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (550,000 bpd), Saudi authorities do not confirm; coalition says it intercepted 2 Ansar Allah ballistic missiles toward Riyadh on Tuesday afternoon

totw_analysis: Our read: '550,000 BARRELS IN THE CROSSHAIRS' -- the Ansar Allah claim a missile fire at Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery; Riyadh says it stopped 2 missiles aimed at the capital. Claim, non-confirmation and the contained-fire report all on screen, nothing asserted beyond them. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Hit or hype: did a Ansar Allah missile actually set Ras Tanura alight, or is an unconfirmed claim plus a contained terminal fire being read as a refinery strike?
